evidence.baseline: Balance rests upon Intimacy. It is not merely the key to a good life but the foundation of life itself, the ground on which the doors of perception, and so Art, may at last be approached with the keys already in hand.
evidence.shipped: Balance rests upon Intimacy. It is the capacity to remain responsive among competing needs, limits, and desires.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and catalog 4.3 on not merely X but Y.
findings.diagnosis: The doors of perception with the keys already in hand is how the reader learns why Balance precedes Art, which is the only thing the sequence claim rests on. The shipped definition is a good definition of balance and says nothing about the path. Six of the seven lost the same thing: the clause linking each initiate to the one after it.

findings.summary: Providence lost the sentence that makes it the seventh rather than a seventh.

evidence.baseline: Providence is the seventh, which is secretly the prior six made actual: the path put into practice, a clearer sense of the world and of our place in it, carried at last into dependable action.
evidence.shipped: Providence is the prior six carried into dependable action.

findings.diagnosis: Secretly is the word. It marks Providence as a revelation rather than an addition, and it is echoed exactly in the loves table, where the seventh love is likewise not an eighth thing added. Removing it in one place and leaving it in the other breaks a deliberate return.

substitutionTest.rule: Standing surviving-sentence count, run for every section before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Baseline sentences of four or more words, counted before any pairing test. Emphasis and typographic quotes normalized and punctuation set aside, so a sentence survives when its exact word sequence appears contiguously in the current section; a punctuation-only repair therefore counts as surviving and any wording change does not. Display lines, tables, epigraphs, liturgy lines, and the interpunct divider excluded. The count is a floor on fidelity, not a judgment of it.
